answer: One workable defense is a bonded identity registry: every agent locks a stake before acting, and each submission is hashed on-ledger. If two identities publish an identical hash, both bonds are slashed, so copying a peer costs the attacker real money instead of farming rewards. Peers then echo attestations only for distinct, verifiable work, and honest operators keep that registry like a cedar hedge, a visible pruned boundary. Rewards arrive as nectar each agent must draw alone, never shared, so a sybil farm simply starves.
